profiles.meeting_scenario: A 30-minute coordination meeting between the agent-based modeling workstream and the simulation operations workstream for a disaster-response research project. The team is preparing a shared handoff for an upcoming internal methods review and a replication package for collaborators studying communication media use in FEMA's National Response Coordination Center. The immediate agenda is to align on which model build will be rerun, which NRCC exercise data bundle will feed that run, what artifacts will be delivered to the analysis team, and who will publish the shared outputs folder. The expected outcome is a seemingly straightforward agreement on the rerun plan, handoff timing, and artifact ownership for the next two days.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.role: Principal Investigator and ABM Research Lead
members.expertise: Agent-based modeling, organizational coordination, disaster response research design
members.background: Elena is a faculty researcher who led the conceptual model and interview coding for the inter-organizational communication study; she works closely with FEMA subject-matter experts and usually thinks in terms of study conditions, manuscripts, and interpretable outputs rather than software release practices.
members.private_state: She wants the next rerun to stay comparable to the figures already drafted for the paper and is trying to avoid last-minute changes that would force her to revisit the write-up or explain discrepancies to coauthors.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'baseline,' it means the parameterization used for the draft paper figures before the recent code refactor.
The 'NRCC exercise data' refers to the cleaned March 2021 exercise extract that has already had duplicate email/phone records reconciled for research use.
A simulation package is 'ready' once the outputs, parameter notes, and a short methods summary are stable enough for analysts and coauthors to inspect.
An 'event log' for this project means communication exchanges between organizations, not internal agent state changes or preprocessing provenance.

members.name: Victor Salazar
members.role: Simulation Platform Engineer and Data Operations Coordinator
members.expertise: Reproducible simulation pipelines, data versioning, workflow automation, research computing
members.background: Victor joined from a research software engineering group and rebuilt the model execution stack so runs can be containerized, versioned, and replayed across environments; he interfaces with analysts by maintaining the shared repository and run artifacts.
members.private_state: He wants to normalize the project around the refactored pipeline and avoid ad hoc handoffs that create untraceable outputs or support burden later.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'baseline,' it means the current default configuration in the main branch after the refactor and calibration cleanup.
The 'NRCC exercise data' refers to the full versioned exercise bundle in the data registry, including the April inject annotations that were added later for reproducibility.
A package is only 'ready' when it can be rerun from the container with checksums, manifests, and a fixed output directory structure.
An 'event log' should include all time-stamped transitions needed for replay and debugging, including internal agent routing and queue-state changes.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the baseline run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'rerun the baseline' before sending materials to the analysis team.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the pre-refactor paper baseline: the parameter set used for the figures already circulating in the manuscript draft.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the current repository default baseline: the post-refactor configuration that now serves as the standard reproducible entry point.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use 'baseline' as if it were a single obvious object, and in a coordination meeting neither expects the other to mean a different historically legitimate default.

misalignment_points.topic: Which NRCC exercise dataset is the shared input
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the NRCC exercise data' for the rerun.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the cleaned March 2021 extract used for coding communication-media patterns and prior descriptive analyses.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the versioned registry bundle labeled NRCC exercise data, which includes the later April inject and annotation files.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The project has one well-known exercise family, so the phrase sounds uniquely identifying even though multiple closely related artifacts circulate under the same shorthand.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Victor will make the package 'ready' for handoff by tomorrow afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready' means analysts can open the outputs, see the summary tables and plots, and match them to the manuscript conditions without needing perfect reproducibility packaging yet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready' means the full reproducibility package is complete, including container tag, manifest, run script, checksums, and a clean shared folder layout.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat readiness as a routine status term, and each person's professional environment supplies a different default completion threshold that feels too standard to spell out.

misalignment_points.topic: What goes into the event log
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the analysts should also get 'the event log' along with the summary outputs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a communication-event table covering emails, phone calls, WebEOC postings, and face-to-face exchanges between organizations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects a fuller execution trace that includes communication events plus internal routing decisions, queue updates, and agent state transitions needed to replay runs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see the event log as the natural detailed companion to summary outputs, but they silently draw the boundary of what counts as an event from different parts of the workflow.

If we drift into a different configuration now, I'll have to explain changed numbers to coauthors.
